hints: Rearrange the trigonometric equation $6\sin^2\theta = 2 + \sin\theta$ to set it equal to zero, forming a standard quadratic in $\sin\theta$.
Factorise the quadratic $6\sin^2\theta - \sin\theta - 2 = 0$ into $(2\sin\theta + 1)(3\sin\theta - 2) = 0$ to find two possible values for $\sin\theta$.
Solve $\sin\theta = -\frac{1}{2}$ and $\sin\theta = \frac{2}{3}$ within the specified interval $-180^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$, identifying angles in all four quadrants.
walkthrough:
Rearrange the equation into a standard 3-term quadratic in $\sin\theta$:
$$6\sin^2\theta = 2 + \sin\theta \implies 6\sin^2\theta - \sin\theta - 2 = 0$$

Factorise the quadratic equation into two linear factors:
$$(2\sin\theta + 1)(3\sin\theta - 2) = 0 \implies \sin\theta = -\frac{1}{2} \quad\text{or}\quad \sin\theta = \frac{2}{3}$$

For $\sin\theta = -\frac{1}{2}$, find angles in the third and fourth quadrants within $-180^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$:
$$\theta = -30^\circ \quad\text{and}\quad \theta = -180^\circ - (-30^\circ) = -150^\circ$$

For $\sin\theta = \frac{2}{3}$, calculate the basic acute angle $\alpha = \arcsin\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) \approx 41.81^\circ$ and find angles in the first and second quadrants:
$$\theta = 41.8^\circ \quad\text{and}\quad \theta = 180^\circ - 41.81^\circ = 138.2^\circ$$

List all four solutions in ascending order:
$$\theta = -150^\circ,\ -30^\circ,\ 41.8^\circ,\ 138.2^\circ$$
